mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following a federal funds rate decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which could negatively impact consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to lower S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods following a 0.2pp increase in unemployment, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real sales (RSAFS) indicates stronger consumer demand, which may boost corporate revenues and drive up S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following a RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests reduced economic activity, which could lead to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods following an INDPRO decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP (GDPC1) coupled with an increase in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods following a decline in GDP and increase in unemployment, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) may lead to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods following a CPI increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) suggests a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following a PAYEMS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates stronger demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following a HOUST increase, the hypothesis is rejected.
